b2b:federation-transport-link.bay:description: Airlock gateways dial outbound to standing relay cells over circuit-relay-v2; the rendezvous control frame, the transport identity it carries, the relay-client certificate plane and the blind rendezvous key are the contracts both ends implement. The fabric keeps N-1 availability (loss of any one provider cell leaves an otherwise authorized exchange unblocked while two healthy cells stay reachable), dials ordered relay candidates under pre-existing bounded failover, and admits only proven end-to-end circuit evidence as circuit-relay-v2 success.

bay:evidence.bay:description: Three standing provider cells (GCP, AWS, Azure); loss of any one cell must not prevent an otherwise authorized exchange while two healthy cells remain reachable. Authorization stays fail-closed: unauthorized exchanges never proceed regardless of cell health.

Gateways and x-mesh hold up to three ordered signed relay candidates, walk them in authority order, replace unhealthy reservations inside their pre-existing bounded retry, and preserve unrelated healthy streams when one relay dial fails. This codifies existing downstream semantics; it defines no new failover algorithm.

Four distinct ordered readiness levels, each necessary but insufficient for the next: l4_reachable (TCP connect only), relay_ready (local relay process readiness), reservation_ready (authenticated unexpired reservation), circuit_proven (completed end-to-end circuit with the inner identity pin verified).

Only circuit_proven satisfies circuit-relay-v2 readiness. Bare TCP connect — including reachability of legacy TLS forwarders — is never success evidence; presentation and CI must not claim circuit-relay-v2 success from TCP reachability alone.

Implementation consumers, identified without prescribing their internals: xx-mesh-net (candidate reservation, bounded failover, circuit dialing), xx-federation-gateway (ordered dialing and evidence presentation), xx-federation-relay (local readiness and reservation truth), xx-sim-infra (two-cell survivability and readiness evidence; container topology unchanged: AWS Fargate only, Azure containers only, GCP serverless org services), xx-builders-portal (readiness presentation shows circuit evidence, never TCP-only success).
Length-prefixed JSON register/submit/deliver/established/error frames exchanged on the outer mTLS connection before the payload-blind splice.
Gateway transport identity, bootstrap server, policy and AES-GCM relay frame types embedded in the control frame and pinned by the inner mTLS handshake.
SPIFFE namespaces and certificate planes for relay-client, relay-cell-server and backplane identities, enforced by both gateway and forwarder.
Receiver rendezvous id and HMAC presence-ref derivation that sender, receiver and forwarder must compute identically.

b2b:control-facade-link.bay:description: Gateways call the local control plane via the narrow FederationService facade only; the facade IDL, its state and failure vocabularies, the receiver intake policy, the registration envelope schema, the certificate provider contract and the pool lease vocabulary are the contracts both sides implement.

bay:evidence.bay:description: FederationService, GatewayRegistrationService and FederationAdminService with their request and response messages (package builders.v1).
ErrorInfo and shared messages imported by federation.proto.
Outbound exchange state and failure classes carried in RecordOutboundExchangeResult, partner-binding field matchers, dev-mode gateway metadata keys.
Partner-link, gateway, credential, trust-root, health and routing-policy state strings carried by facade views, with the usability predicates both sides evaluate.
Receiver-owned intake and data-channel postures resolved by the gateway at intake and administered by control.
relay-mesh-registration.v0 command and response envelopes, bootstrap intents and local-control authorizations exchanged during join ceremonies.
Certificate issue, rotate and revoke requests, CSR parsing and identity evidence shared by the gateway and the control-plane registration server.
Coordinator lease kind and liveness rule applied by control when leasing and by the gateway router when selecting a path.

b2b:agent-bidi-stream.bay:description: Workstation agents connect to control plane over ConnectAgent / ConnectRuntime. The control owns the run/task/event/attachment ledger and ordered observation stream; agents join as authenticated Agent Kit container participants with immutable runtime provenance; attachment fetch and return happen by scoped capability carrying refs only, never bytes. Relays stay payload-blind: no orchestration semantics are added to relay cells.

bay:evidence.bay:description: Run/task/event lifecycle, typed event vocabulary, server-assigned sequence and visibility, tenant-scoped cursors, and the audit hash chain both sides implement.
Run, participant, and task records with team shape (one PM, parallel builders, different-agent reviewer), task DAG, and sanitized explicit summaries; never chain-of-thought or raw reasoning.
Content-addressed attachment refs and scoped fetch/return capabilities with fail-closed fetch-target, digest, MIME, size, and decompression guards.
Immutable OCI, Agent Kit, CLI, model, provider, network-policy, and spec evidence verified against pins with container-only placement (GCP Cloud Run, Azure ACA/ACI, AWS ECS Fargate-only).

b2b:client-rpc-link.bay:description: Next.js Portal calls builders-control on gRPC :9090 with zero direct SQL. The portal sends BFF command/query envelopes and reads the typed observation projection with cursor-resumed watch; browser actor identity comes from the authenticated control context, never request fields, and every reply carries a signed audit receipt or an explicit degraded/incomplete status.

bay:evidence.bay:description: Idempotent start/cancel/query envelopes with context-resolved actors and Ed25519-signed audit receipts.
Server-assigned visibility, sanitized bounded summaries, the explicit partner-safe allowlist, and gap-free resumable reads that report degraded/incomplete instead of silent success.
Attachment refs as observation evidence only: opaque ids, digests, sizes, sniffed MIME, and audience binding; no bytes, paths, storage URLs, secrets, or capability values in events.
OrchestrationService BFF surface (StartRun, CancelRun, GetRun, WatchEvents) with run, participant, task, event, provenance, attachment, and partner projection messages.

Revision 7 (issue #3 item 3): give the gateway-facing wire and facade contracts a machine-readable home in this repository. Declares contract artifacts for the gateway-to-gateway transport and relay rendezvous wire types (contracts/transport, contracts/relaywire), the federation state, org-registry rendezvous/intake and facade vocabularies (contracts/federationstate, contracts/orgregistry, contracts/facade), the gateway registration envelope schema, certificate plane vocabulary and gateway pool lease vocabulary moved from xx-federation-gateway (gatewayregistration, gatewaycert, gatewaypool), and the FederationService/GatewayRegistrationService/FederationAdminService IDL projected as api/proto/builders/v1/{federation,common}.proto at the xx-builders-net origin/dev c1ad78a bytes (includes the portal S1 read RPCs and ErrorInfo domain/reason fields). Repoints rel.gateway-dials-relay and rel.gateway-connects-control from monorepo-relative source-pointers to those contracts and attaches evidence. Adds api/proto/builders/v1/{federation,common}.proto to bay:delivery as generated projections and bumps metadata version to 1.5.0 (recorded in this summary, as change-set.b2b-002 did for 1.1.0, because operation target-refs must be declared ids). No component fields change. PM decisions: D1 gatewaycert moved wholesale with package name kept (contracts-safe tests only; store-resolver binding and command-graph guard stay in the gateway repo); D2 the facade IDL is owned authoritatively here (source bytes traced to the control commit above) and downstream generates outward from this repo — scripts/check-projections.py enforces the offline projection-artifact-digest link plus an outward-only export, and refuses any reverse generator; D3 catrust.LoadComposableCAPool stays gateway-local; transport.Negotiator.Metrics is a one-method MetricsRecorder interface; orgregistry.PresenceRef takes canonical input and fails closed (CanonicalDomain stays gateway-local, needs x/net/idna). Deliberate fail-closed hardenings owned by this repository (divergences from the pre-move bodies, each pinned by tests): length-delimited AES-GCM AAD, sanitized public transport errors with local-only diagnostic causes, production intake gated on RegistrationEligibilityForOrgStatus, DNS-SAN-bound server-auth plane verification with wildcard rejection, cryptographic identity binding (SPIFFE/fingerprint) in MatchesExpectedIdentity, and deny-by-default GatewayAllowedByIdentity with an explicit AllowAllGateways sentinel. External federation certificate planes use their own declared SPIFFE namespaces, never the internal builders-net trust domain (see artifact.contracts.gatewaycert-planes). All artifact digests are real SHA-256 values, no placeholders.

Revision 8 (issue #15): define the N-1 relay-cell availability and machine-verifiable readiness contract as one atomic unit. Adds contracts/relayavailability (artifact.contracts.relayavailability): 3 standing provider cells with a 2-healthy minimum so loss of any one cell leaves an otherwise authorized exchange unblocked; up to 3 ordered signed relay candidates walked in authority order with unhealthy reservations replaced inside pre-existing bounded retry (codifies existing xx-mesh-net semantics, no new algorithm); four ordered readiness levels (l4_reachable, relay_ready, reservation_ready, circuit_proven); only circuit_proven satisfies circuit-relay-v2 readiness so bare TCP connect is never success evidence; fail-closed authorization and candidate selection throughout. Attaches five evidence entries to rel.gateway-dials-relay (revision 2 to 3) and identifies downstream consumers xx-mesh-net, xx-federation-gateway, xx-federation-relay, xx-sim-infra and xx-builders-portal without prescribing their internals. No XSD change required (evidence plus contract artifact under the existing model); no proto projection change; sim-infra pure-container fields untouched (AWS Fargate only, Azure containers only, GCP serverless org services); no cloud, DNS, certificate, credential or deployment action. Bumps metadata version to 1.6.0. All artifact digests are real SHA-256 values, no placeholders.

Adds contracts/orchestration (run/participant/task/event model with 15 typed lifecycle kinds; fail-closed ledger with server-assigned sequence/visibility, tenant-scoped cursors, duplicate-terminal rejection, and audit hash chain; sanitized bounded summaries with an explicit partner-safe allowlist; BFF command/query envelopes with idempotent start, context-resolved actors, cursor-resumed watch, degraded/incomplete status, and signed audit receipts), contracts/attachment (content-addressed refs with scoped fetch/return capabilities and fail-closed target/digest/MIME/size/decompression guards; events carry refs only, never bytes), contracts/provenance (immutable OCI/Agent Kit/CLI/model/provider/network-policy/spec evidence with pin verification and container-only placement), and the OrchestrationService formal API contract artifact api/proto/builders/v1/orchestration.proto (linked and digested in this seal; the Go packages enforce it and scripts/check-orchestration-consistency.py proves XML, proto, and Go agree, so neither the proto nor the Go is a second unlinked schema). Updates comp.builders-control (revision 2 to 3: orchestration/attachment ledger), comp.builders-agent (2 to 3: Agent Kit container participant mode and runtime provenance), comp.builders-portal (3 to 4: typed observation projection and BFF evidence only), comp.sim-infra (4 to 5: orchestration runtime vocabulary for GCP Cloud Run and Azure ACA/ACI with AWS ECS Fargate-only), rel.agent-connects-control (1 to 2: orchestration/telemetry/attachment-capability/provenance evidence) and rel.portal-dials-control (1 to 2: BFF/observation-stream/attachment-evidence/IDL evidence). Exact-head review fixes sealed in the same unit: real run/task lifecycle transitions validated through AllowedRunTransition/AllowedTaskTransition with run/task scope framing, transactional append (pure plan, stamp, append, commit), hardened SSRF fetch-target validation (canonical dots, local suffixes, single-label and numeric-TLD denial, decimal/octal/hex/4-in-6 IP forms, decoded traversal, silent denials) with connect-time resolved-IP revalidation, enforced active-content blocking at reference and body verification, and trimmed task-summary comparison. Extends schemas/b2b-architecture-v1.xsd to 1.3.0 with additive optional fields and scripts/validate-spec.py with the orchestration seal gate (artifacts, evidence, fields, container-only cloud vocabulary, spec privacy). Adds deterministic Markdown/HTML catalog projections under projections/ with a clean-diff gate. Bumps metadata version to 1.7.0 (recorded in this summary, as change-set.b2b-002 did for 1.1.0, because operation target-refs must be declared ids). No XSD change required beyond the additive fields; no cloud, DNS, certificate, credential, product runtime, or deployment action. All artifact digests are real SHA-256 values, no placeholders.
